speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; you mentioned episodes of dizziness and vertigo, can you describe what those episodes feel like and how long they last?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the position-dependence of your vertigo is a key finding. Given your age and hearing loss, are you experiencing any ringing in your ears (tinnitus) or hearing fluctuations alongside these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The history of position-dependent vertigo in a 70-year-old with presbycusis is classic for BPPV; I recommend an Epley maneuver to confirm and treat.
